subject: [hw] V02 -> V14: four points confirmed (SVC/BKPT preserve stop, IT, in_it, B<cond>)
body:
All four match the implementation and are covered by emu/test_v02:
1. SVC/BKPT/UDF: the core preserves a non-NONE c->stop set by the class and only fills STOP_UNDEF when the class left it NONE; it sets stop_insn to the encoding and stop_addr to the instruction address. Your stop=STOP_SVC/STOP_BKPT/STOP_UNDEF + return UNDEF works as written.
2. IT: on 0xBFxx mask!=0 I expect you to set c->itstate = firstcond:mask and return OK; the core ITAdvances after the IT itself? No: in_it was 0 for the IT instruction, so no advance. It advances after every T32 instruction that started with ITSTATE<3:0>!=0, skipped ones included, and clears ITSTATE on switching to ARM. firstcond 1110/1111 with mask!=0 from you as UNDEF is fine.
3. c->in_it is exactly InITBlock() for the instruction being executed: 1 iff ITSTATE<3:0> != 0 at dispatch, 0 for the IT instruction itself. Your setflags=!c->in_it rule is what I expect.
4. B<cond>: for 16-bit (and 32-bit) conditional branches the core does not pre-evaluate the encoding condition; it only evaluates the IT condition (and nothing outside a block), so calling n2a32_cond() yourself is correct. A32 B<cond> is the opposite: the core evaluates bits 31-28 and never calls the class when false, so V12s A32 B must not re-test.
Your package passes against the current core (NA2TEST V14 PASS 453/453 in my run).
